blockMcqs.question: Which two controls form the core of database access security?
blockMcqs.explanation: Authentication proves identity; authorization decides what that identity may do. All other controls build on these two.

blockMcqs.question: A valid token is presented but access is still denied. Which step failed?
blockMcqs.explanation: The token proved identity (authentication passed), but the permission check (authorization) rejected the action.

blockMcqs.question: What does RBAC assign to users instead of individual permissions?
blockMcqs.explanation: RBAC bundles permissions into roles and assigns roles to users, making bulk grant/revoke simple.

blockMcqs.question: An app only reads orders. Least privilege says it should have:
options: SELECT on the orders table only
INSERT and DELETE on all tables
No permissions — read from a cache
blockMcqs.explanation: Least privilege means granting exactly what the app needs — SELECT on orders — and nothing more.

blockMcqs.question: SQL injection works because user input is treated as:
blockMcqs.explanation: When input is concatenated into a query string, the DB parses it as SQL — so injected keywords alter the query's logic.

blockMcqs.question: Why do parameterized queries stop SQL injection?
options: They encrypt the query before sending
They send the value and query structure separately
They strip all special characters automatically
They log the query for review
blockMcqs.explanation: The driver sends SQL structure and the value in separate channels; the DB treats the value as data only, never as syntax.

blockMcqs.question: Which threat does encryption in transit (TLS) specifically address?
options: Network eavesdropping between app and DB
blockMcqs.explanation: TLS wraps the connection, protecting data in motion from being read by a network attacker. Disk theft is covered by encryption at rest.

blockMcqs.question: Why store audit logs in a separate write-only destination?
options: To speed up queries on the main DB
So an attacker who owns the DB cannot erase the trail
Because the DB engine requires it
blockMcqs.explanation: If logs live on the same system, a full compromise lets the attacker cover their tracks. A separate write-only store preserves the audit trail.

blockMcqs.question: Which common mistake directly violates least privilege?
options: Enabling TLS on the DB connection
Granting DBA role to an app account for easy setup
blockMcqs.explanation: Granting DBA to an app gives far more permission than needed, violating least privilege and massively expanding the blast radius.
